subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Space Elevators: The Impossible Infrastructure
description: A 60-second lesson on Space Elevators: The Impossible Infrastructure.

hook.text: A cable from Earth's surface to geostationary orbit would eliminate the need for rockets. The concept is a space elevator.

buildup.text: Arthur C. Clarke popularized the idea in 1979. A counterweight beyond GEO keeps the cable taut through centrifugal force.

discovery.text: No material on Earth is strong enough. The cable must support its own weight over 35,786 km. Carbon nanotubes might work.

twist.text: A lunar space elevator is feasible with existing materials. The Moon's lower gravity makes the engineering far easier.

climax.text: Researchers continue developing stronger materials. If carbon nanotubes can be made in long strands, the elevator becomes real.

punchline.text: The physics works. The materials don't exist. Yet.

quiz.question: What is the main barrier preventing construction of a space elevator?
options: The cost of construction exceeds all current global space budgets combined
No known material is strong enough to support a cable spanning 35,786 km under its own weight
Space debris would sever the cable within days of it being deployed
